capacity_model.h5_logical_formula: 40 * frames * particles + 8 * frames + 13 * particles bytes before HDF5 metadata/filter effects
capacity_model.h5_logical_components: per frame/particle: valid 1 + position 12 + velocity 12 + density 4 + mass 4 + pressure 4 + type 1 + mk 2 = 40 bytes; fixed arrays: time 8*frames and particle_id/zone/initial_type/initial_mk/initial_mass = 13*particles
capacity_model.conservative_home_incremental_bound: For a new conversion, Home output cannot be proven below 32 GiB from source alone: runtime reserves 32 GiB, the wrapper publishes a staged H5 by verified copy to a Home .partial then os.replace, and PartVTK CSV/report temporaries are on the attempt tree. Do not substitute observed compressed H5 sizes for this guard.
capacity_model.staging_bound: NVMe wrapper enforces staged H5 <= 24 GiB and requires 100 GiB free; this is a staging bound, not a Home reservation reduction.
capacity_model.csv_bound: PartVTK writes one selected-frame CSV at a time and deletes it when keep_validation_csv is false, but the code has no byte cap; observed CSV stats are diagnostics only, so a complete conservative future CSV upper bound is unproven.
capacity_model.decoder_scratch_bound: Per-frame decoder scratch is reclaimed after each decode, but decoder XML/auxiliary output has no source-level byte cap; complete peak is unproven. The wrapper does not change this scratch location.
capacity_model.global_home_peak: Unprovable from this snapshot because pre-existing data, reservations, concurrent consumers, and dynamic ledger state can change; the live Root142 Home-floor guard remains authoritative.
